id: Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead (1995)
title: Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead
tagline: One last job. One cold drink.
about: A reformed crook pulls together an old crew for one last job that goes wrong.
cue: Serve the drinks when the Man With The Plan calls in Jimmy's debt.
faces: One mile above the sea, give or take a barstool.
Our view west. City Park to the mountains.
Rum, pineapple, coconut cream, blended. Umbrella.
Two rums, orange curaçao, almond syrup, lime.
Rum, blue curaçao, pineapple, cream of coconut.
Three rums, lime, grapefruit. Limit two a night.
Tell us your day. We pour to match it.
Pick a title. Lingo is free here. Rum is not.
Every crew round gets a toast from the bar.
The Man with the Plan gets the corner table.
Mister Shhh drinks alone. Let him.
Say it on tape for the ones you leave behind.
Six halves, yolks whipped with Dijon and pickle juice, smoked paprika, chives.
Melted white cheese, roasted green chiles, garlic, cumin. Corn chips to dunk.
Thin beef patty, Swiss and slow onions on rye, griddled crisp in butter.
Three eggs folded over diced ham, green pepper, onion and cheddar.
Puffed fried pastry pillows, warm honey, a dust of cinnamon.
Fresh pot all night. Booths get topped up first.
The counter. Sugar on every stool, pie under glass. Joe Heff keeps the corner booth.
Critical Bill, Pieces, Franchise, Easy Wind
On my tab, all night. Whatever the boys want.
Afterlife Advice, back hallway. Say your piece to camera in one take. Pick a title, we label the tape.
The Altitude, 1995 E. Colfax Ave., Denver. Form No. 95. No buckwheats on the premises.

Finish with smoked paprika and chopped chives.Green Chile QuesoMelted white cheese, roasted green chiles, garlic, cumin. Serve straight away with the corn chips.MainsPatty MeltThin beef patty, Swiss and slow onions on rye, griddled crisp in butter.The booth where the plan gets made.How to make it2 brown onions, sliced60g butter600g beef mince8 slices of rye bread8 slices of Swiss cheesesalt and pepper, to tasteCook the onions in a little of the butter over low heat until soft and golden.Shape the mince into 4 thin oval patties, season, and sear in a hot pan until browned on both sides.Butter the bread on the outside. Build each sandwich with a patty, onions and two slices of Swiss cheese.Griddle the sandwiches in a pan over medium heat, turning once, until crisp and the cheese has melted.SweetsSopapillasPuffed fried pastry pillows, warm honey, a dust of cinnamon.Pick a title. Rub in the butter, then add the warm water and mix to a soft dough.Rest the dough, covered, so it relaxes.Roll the dough out 3mm thick and cut into 16 squares.Fry in batches in oil heated to 180°C for about a minute a side, until puffed and golden.
